snippet.textDisplay: Did you know Jesus already forgave you of all your past, present, and future sins? (Colossians 2:13-14, 2 Corinthians 5:18-19, Hebrews 10:18, 1 John 2:12). The problem is we still view ourselves as an unholy, imperfect sinner, even though the Bible says we are now holy and perfected forever (Hebrews 10:10; 14). That's because it was always about His obedience that stood between you and heaven. Not yours. Romans 5:19 "For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous." 2 Corinthians 5:21 "God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God." All God wants from you is to believe that Jesus saved you from your sins, and you will have eternal life (John 8:24, Acts 16:31, Romans 3:19-28, John 3:16-18, 1 Corinthians 15:1-5, Ephesians 1:13-14). You never have to fear going to hell again, because Titus 2:11-12 says it's the grace of God that teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts and live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age. Notice what teaches us… GRACE. Not the fear of losing salvation. Not the threat of eternal condemnation. Not an angry God waiting to punish you... GRACE. When you understand what Jesus did for you, you begin to see life a lot differently. You're no longer trying to earn something from God. You're learning to live in accordance with who you already are in Christ. Does that mean you'll never struggle with sin again? Of course not. The Bible teaches that we will continue to sin and fall into temptation (1 John 2:1, Romans 7:14-25). The only difference is the grace and blood of Jesus covers it now (Romans 5:20-21, Ephesians 1:7, Matthew 26:28, Hebrews 9:22). But grace was never intended to make us comfortable with sin. It teaches us to live differently. Instead of sinning however we want, we do not want to grieve the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 4:30). We should desire to "live a life worthy of the Lord and please him in every way." (Colossians 1:10). We don't obey God to become His children. We already belong to Him, so we are learning to live as His children (John 1:12-13). 🤍
